text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with eight quote variants for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: Between 2019 and 2023, rainfall in the Keravi Plateau fell below the long-term average in four of five growing seasons. Smallholder households that relied on hybrid maize lost an estimated 38 percent of their harvest during the worst year. The Tamsin Seed Collective began trialling sorghum, pearl millet and cowpea varieties with 240 farmers in 2021. Early results were encouraging: drought-tolerant plots yielded nearly twice as much grain as conventional plots under the same conditions. However, the trials did not include women-headed households, who make up roughly one third of the plateau's farming population. Local seed banks have never stocked certified drought-resilient varieties in sufficient quantity. This proposal seeks funding to expand the trials to 900 households across three sub-counties.

variants.changed_quantity: rainfall in the Keravi Plateau fell below the long-term average in three of five growing seasons.
variants.added_negation: drought-tolerant plots never yielded nearly twice as much grain as conventional plots under the same conditions.
variants.removed_negation: However, the trials include women-headed households, who make up roughly one third of the plateau's farming population.
variants.reordered: Early results were encouraging: conventional plots yielded nearly twice as much grain as drought-tolerant plots under the same conditions.
variants.paraphrase: Village seed stores have always lacked enough certified drought-tolerant seed.

passages.source_passage: Since the last board meeting, the Saltmarsh Early Warning Programme has installed 14 siren towers along the Orrin coast, bringing the total to 31. Village response committees ran evacuation drills in 22 communities during March and April. Average time to reach designated shelters fell from 47 minutes to 29 minutes. The SMS alert system was tested on 3 May and reached 86% of registered phones within ten minutes. Not every result was positive. Two committees in the Brenmouth estuary have not met since January, and their drills were postponed. Staff also report that elderly residents living alone weren't reliably reached by door-to-door volunteers. The management team recommends that the board approve a modest reallocation of the contingency budget to recruit additional volunteers before the cyclone season begins in November.

passages.source_passage: The Halvern District Disability Forum estimates that 6,200 residents live with a mobility, visual or hearing impairment, yet only 410 own an appropriate assistive device. A 2022 household survey by the Forum found that 58 percent of disabled adults had not visited a health facility in the previous year, most often citing inaccessible transport. None of the district's eleven secondary schools has a ramp at its main entrance. Repair services are scarce: wheelchairs that break are usually abandoned because spare parts are sold only in the capital. Since 2020, Openway Mobility has trained six local technicians to fit and repair devices. This proposal builds on that work by establishing a district workshop and an accessibility audit programme for public buildings.

passages.source_passage: During the second quarter of 2024, the Brightway Vocational Centre in Lussa enrolled 168 trainees across its tailoring, welding, solar installation and catering courses. Female enrolment reached 44 percent, up from 31 percent in the first quarter. Attendance averaged 87 percent, although the welding course lost nine trainees who moved to seasonal farm work. Of the 120 graduates from the January cohort, 73 were in paid employment or self-employment three months after completion. The centre did not meet its target for apprenticeship placements, securing only 19 against a target of 40. Employers in the Lussa industrial zone said they were not aware of the programme, and the placement officer post remained vacant for six weeks.

passages.source_passage: The mid-term evaluation of the Clearspring Rural Water Project covered 18 villages in the Marabou valley between July and September 2023. Of the 25 boreholes planned, 21 have been drilled and 19 are functional; two failed because the water table was lower than predicted. Household latrine coverage rose from 34 percent at baseline to 61 percent. Evaluators found that water user committees in most villages collect fees, but none has yet saved enough to replace a hand pump. Handwashing stations were present at only a minority of latrines inspected. Women interviewed said they no longer walk more than an hour to collect water. The evaluation team did not find evidence of reduced diarrhoeal illness, though clinic records were incomplete.

passages.source_passage: By the end of June 2024, the Ndara Savings Partnership supported 142 village savings and loan associations with 3,480 active members, of whom 78 percent are women. Cumulative savings reached the equivalent of 96,000 US dollars, and the average loan size was 41 dollars. Loan repayment remained strong at 94 percent. Most loans financed petty trade, livestock and school fees. Eleven groups did not hold a share-out this cycle because their records were incomplete, and field officers have not yet audited them. Membership growth slowed in the northern cluster, where a cattle market closure reduced household income. No group reported theft of its cash box during the quarter, compared with three incidents in the previous quarter.

passages.source_passage: In 2023, the Kivule District Community Health Programme deployed 312 community health workers across 64 villages in the highlands of western Tanzara. Each worker visited an average of 28 households per month, screening children for malnutrition and referring pregnant women for antenatal care. Facility deliveries in programme villages rose to 71 percent, compared with 52 percent in 2021. We did not achieve the target for childhood immunisation, which stalled at 80 percent because of a vaccine stock-out in the third quarter. Stipends were paid late in four of twelve months, and nineteen workers left the programme. Community health workers are not authorised to dispense antibiotics, so pneumonia cases still require referral to a health centre several kilometres away.

passages.source_passage: Smallholder farmers in the Ombele lowlands cultivate an average of 1.2 hectares, mostly cassava, groundnuts and rice. Extension services are thin: one government officer serves roughly 2,500 farming households. In 2018 the Greenfurrow Trust launched farmer field schools, where groups of about 25 farmers test practices on a shared demonstration plot over a full season. By 2023 the network had grown to 86 schools. Participants adopted mulching and line planting at higher rates than neighbours, but most schools have never had access to improved rice seed. Women attend regularly, yet they rarely hold leadership roles, and only nine schools are chaired by a woman. The proposed project would not replace government extension; it would link field schools to district agronomists and seed suppliers.

passages.source_passage: Between January and March 2024, the case management team in Sector C of the Alder Ridge camp opened 237 new protection cases and closed 158. Unaccompanied and separated children accounted for 41 percent of new cases, and survivors of gender-based violence for a further 22 percent. Caseworkers completed initial assessments within 72 hours for most high-risk cases. However, 14 high-risk cases did not receive a follow-up visit within the required two weeks, largely because two caseworker posts were vacant. Interpretation remains a constraint: no staff member currently speaks Lirrhani, the language of about one in ten new arrivals. Referrals to the camp's mental health service increased, but the service has not added counselling capacity since last year.

passages.source_passage: The mid-term evaluation of the Fairpath Paralegal Outreach Service reviewed activity from April 2022 to March 2024 in the districts of Corran and Velde. Thirty-two community paralegals handled 2,915 cases, most concerning land disputes, inheritance and unpaid wages. Around 63 percent of cases were resolved through mediation without going to court. Clients interviewed valued the paralegals' availability on market days and said they would not have sought help from a lawyer. The evaluators noted that paralegals in Velde lacked a reliable referral pathway to qualified advocates. Case files were incomplete in a sample of 120 records, and the service has never conducted a systematic follow-up of clients after resolution. Funding for paralegal stipends ends in December 2024.
